bottom_line: The gauge read 4.2 m at noon, after rising 0.3 m since the morning — will it pass the 4.6 m record from 2009?

headline.dek: Above the 4.0 m flood mark, but short of the 2009 high of 4.6 m.
headline.title: The river gauge passes the flood threshold

scenes.question: How high is the river?
scenes.why: The 4.2 m reading means little on its own — on an axis against the 4.0 m threshold and the 4.6 m record, the reader sees at a glance how close the town is to trouble.

data.speaker: Mara Ellison
data.text: We watch the gauge, not the sky.

scenes.question: How does the town decide when to worry?
scenes.why: One line that carries the story's stance: the gauge, not the weather, is what the town watches.
